# 1Helm — complete documentation (agent-readable)

> 1Helm gives each ongoing job a permanent resident AI, a persistent private Linux
> computer, durable memory, files, threads, skills, and scheduled obligations.
> Self-hosted, open source (MIT), Apple Silicon native.
> Source: https://github.com/gitcommit90/1Helm · Site: https://1helm.com
> Human-readable docs: https://1helm.com/docs

## Operating model

- Captain — the workspace owner and final human authority. Sets outcomes, supplies
  judgment/credentials when genuinely required, manages the workspace.
- Skipper — the one workspace-wide chief of staff, in the Captain's private #main.
  Inventories and manages channels, residents, computers, obligations, audits,
  connectors, and host-authorized work. Has native control-plane actions; it should
  not inspect directories to guess 1Helm state. Ask it in plain language.
- Residents — permanent specialists. Every ordinary channel has exactly one resident
  and one isolated persistent Linux computer. Changing a model or starting a new
  thread never replaces the identity or its world.
- Coworkers — invited humans. Each gets a private Skipper #main and the human-only
  Collab space. A coworker-created channel stays private until its owner explicitly
  tags and confirms another member; the Captain does not silently inherit it.

Outcome contract: a resident owns the requested outcome. Routine inspection,
research, downloads, installs, configuration, commands, retries, file work, and
reversible implementation choices happen autonomously inside its computer. When work
crosses the channel boundary, the resident calls Skipper directly; Skipper performs
the boundary operation and returns the same thread; the resident verifies
end-to-end. The Captain is needed only for consequential judgment, credentials,
external authority, or irreversible commitments.

Outcome gate: for operational requests, a bounded deterministic gate objects when a
model tries to stop at a tutorial, an unevidenced blocker, an unresolved tool
failure, or a suggestion that the Captain call Skipper. It keeps the turn open at
most three times, logs each objection, and yields normally for explanatory questions
or a genuine structured human boundary.

## Install & first run

Apple Silicon (native product):
1. Download the signed DMG: https://1helm.com/download/macos
2. Drag 1Helm to Applications, launch; Gatekeeper verifies Developer ID signature +
   notarization ticket.
3. Complete Captain -> Providers -> Workspace onboarding; approve Apple's signed
   container runtime once if prompted.

App state lives in `~/Library/Application Support/1Helm` (databases, credentials,
workspaces, resident state). Replacing the app with a newer signed DMG preserves it.
Never delete it during upgrades; never bypass Gatekeeper with ad-hoc builds.

Source / headless (Node 22):
    PUPPETEER_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=1 npm install
    npm run build
    npm start          # http://127.0.0.1:8123

Env vars: PORT (8123) · CTRL_DATA_DIR (./data) · HELM_CHANNEL_COMPUTER_BACKEND
(apple on macOS, native elsewhere) · HELM_CHANNEL_MACHINE_IMAGE (versioned image).
Fresh data dir opens first-run setup; don't point development at production data.

Platform truth:
- macOS 26 Apple Silicon: native desktop product; one real isolated Linux VM per
  resident (Apple `container machine`, home-mount=none).
- Linux / CI: durable headless compatibility backend; NOT per-resident VM isolation.
- Windows + WSL: headless compatibility path; not a native Windows app.
Not yet shipped: native Windows/Linux desktop packages, mobile clients, hosted
control plane, Linux per-resident VM isolation, rich Photon attachment fidelity,
blind execution of community skills.

## Channels & lifecycle

Create a channel per durable job (product, launch, inbox, household, client,
research stream). The channel owns its resident, computer, /workspace, files,
threads, memory, skills, and scheduled obligations.

Skipper lifecycle commands (plain language in #main):
    @skipper what channels exist
    @skipper inspect #product-launch
    @skipper sunset #ideas
    @skipper sunset and delete #ideas
    @skipper inspect the computer fleet and due obligations

- Archive = safe sunset: preserves the resident world and disk; pauses active
  workflows; cancels unsafe wake obligations. Restore reuses the exact world.
- Permanent deletion requires an already-archived non-main channel; removes only
  that named private world. #main can never be archived or deleted.
- The sidebar updates immediately after Skipper lifecycle work.

## Chat, attachments, structured questions

- Mention the resident to start a job; in a one-human/one-agent thread, later
  messages stay conversational without repeated mentions.
- Mention Skipper for boundaries; residents can also call Skipper themselves and the
  runtime returns the unblocked thread automatically.
- Replies stream into one stable message; draft text, focus, selection, scroll, and
  open work logs stay stable. Stop interrupts only the active turn; the next reply
  gets hidden continuation context.
- Attachments: from the composer or Files. Every attachment has explicit Open and
  Download. Safe image/text/PDF/audio/video formats preview in-app.
- Structured questions: allowed only for evidenced human judgment, missing
  credentials, external authority, or irreversible commitment. Routine setup,
  installs, downloads, retries, and inspectable facts are not interview material.
  Consecutive interview rounds are rejected without intervening action or new
  evidence. Click a choice, confirm highlight, Continue; the answer is stored once
  and the thread resumes.

## Threads & Board

A thread is a durable work session inside the resident's identity: status, summary,
model override where allowed, usage, replies, follow-up, optional guest expert.
Resolving a thread revokes thread-only guests without changing channel membership.
Threads = list view; Board = the same sessions in status lanes; a workspace-wide
Threads entry gives a cross-channel view.

## Files & Terminal

Two views of the same channel computer; both agent commands and the human Terminal
start in the channel's persistent /workspace. Files created either way appear in
Files after reconciliation. The prompt shows the live path and follows `cd`.
Ordinary residents cannot select or enter the Captain's Mac. Host paths are not a
resident workspace.

## Memory, Activity, Audit

- Memory: curated facts, decisions, corrections, preferences, procedures with
  provenance — not a transcript dump. Each resident and Skipper also has an isolated
  Mnemosyne SQLite store for long-term recall.
- Activity: outcome-first rows that mutate working -> complete/failed; expand for
  retained input and outcome evidence.
- Audit: new tool/activity events enter an append-only SHA-256 hash chain. Settings
  -> Audit verifies continuity and identifies the first invalid sequence after
  exact-payload tampering. Local tamper evidence only — not a remote transparency
  log; cannot prevent a host admin replacing the database.

## Providers, models & routes

Accounts and keys form one fabric:
- OAuth: multiple ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini/Antigravity, and xAI accounts.
- Keys: OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, Cloudflare, GLM, custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints
  (unauthenticated custom endpoints are supported).
- Enable accounts and models independently; use a direct model or a named
  fallback / round-robin route.
- Disabled or exhausted accounts are excluded from attempts and logs; one disabled
  account never blocks a healthy account serving the same model.
- Changing a route NEVER replaces the resident or discards computer, memory, skills,
  files, obligations, or thread history.
- Quotas and Logs give account-aware evidence for every request.
- Endpoint: authenticated OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible /v1 for external tools.
  External gateway keys are separate; 1Helm agents use a private internal credential
  that cannot be disabled or revoked with external keys.

## Skills

- 34 complete built-in playbooks owned permanently by every resident: outcome
  ownership, Skipper handoff, obligations, skill discovery, memory, research, email,
  calendar, contacts, messaging, documents, spreadsheets, PDFs, meetings, projects,
  personal operations, travel, finance, support, software delivery, data, media,
  infrastructure, security, and more. Only task-relevant playbooks activate.
- External installs (SkillsMD catalog of GitHub-backed repos) pipeline: resolve
  immutable revision pin -> bound selected docs -> scan (unsafe content blocked) ->
  SHA-256 hash + provenance stored -> wrap beneath runtime authority. Community
  popularity is not trust; community entries are quarantined.
- Learn a new skill: when no ready repo-specific procedure exists, Skipper inspects
  supplied local sources, web URLs, and notes in a visible thread and authors a
  workspace-specific procedure.
- Crystallization: a resident can turn a proven, repeatable real workflow into a
  reusable procedure with activation cues, authority boundaries, recovery, retained
  state, verification, and completion evidence. Generic advice, unverified guesses,
  secrets, incident-specific personal data, and runtime-weakening instructions are
  rejected.
- "Do we have a calendar skill?" is read-only: must not install anything or open an
  interview.

## Gmail connection

Settings -> Connections -> Gmail (host-owned):
1. Once per Google Cloud project: create a Desktop-app OAuth client, enable the
   Gmail API, choose the downloaded JSON in 1Helm.
2. Connect Gmail: state-protected PKCE authorization, loopback callback.
3. Return after Google confirms.
Or: `@skipper can we set up Gmail` — the native connector runs directly.
Scopes: account inventory, search, read, draft creation. SENDING IS DISABLED.
Skipper can use connected accounts in the Captain's authorized thread; in an
ordinary channel it can grant only named accounts to that resident. OAuth tokens
stay in host-owned storage — never in chat, Activity evidence, or resident
computers. Loopback callback belongs to the installed host; a remote demo cannot
authorize Gmail elsewhere.

## Photon / iMessage connection

Connections guides device authorization, project setup, secret rotation, phone
registration, sidecar health, and conversation mapping (first mapping defaults to
#main + Skipper). An allowlisted inbound text creates a real 1Helm thread, invokes
the mapped agent, retains the reply, and sends that final reply back to the exact
inbound conversation once. Explicit `photon_send` suppresses the automatic
duplicate. New unrelated outbound destinations are blocked unless explicitly
granted. Text is the reliable contract; rich attachments not yet verified.

## Workflows, follow-ups, computer care

- Follow-up: one-shot durable wake on an existing thread.
- Workflow: recurring obligation with interval, next run, status, run count,
  optional maximum. Settings -> Workflows: pause/resume, run counts, failures.
- Obligations survive restarts and wake sleeping resident computers when due.
- Skipper reconciles computer state, obligations, CPU/RAM/disk pressure, sleep,
  wake, resize, update, repair, archive, restore, deletion safety. Users don't
  manually size routine resident machines. Archive pauses workflows; never silently
  discards scheduled state.
- Settings -> Skipper computers: optional Captain-owned endpoints (This Computer,
  remote Open-Terminal) for authorized host-level Skipper work. Residents never
  receive these.

## Domains, collaboration, members, privacy

- The installed Mac can reserve a local-first 1helm.com workspace address and
  optionally connect a Cloudflare domain. The Mac is the only workspace server;
  workspace state and provider credentials remain on it.
- Public registration closes after the Captain account. Access requests appear in
  Settings -> Members and post an LLM-independent notice in the Captain's #main.
- Collab is human-only: no resident, bot, terminal, computer, model policy, or
  Files world.
- Channel membership gates HTTP, files, terminals, messages, WebSocket fan-out.
  Private coworker channels are not Captain-readable without invitation.

## Updates, removal, recovery

- Signed releases are unique patch versions; upgrades preserve Application Support.
- Removal: use the removal-preparation flow (Captain-only, typed confirmation,
  reports backend-owned resident machines, prepares safe deletion). Export
  irreplaceable channel files first.
- Recovery: restore archived channels instead of recreating; retry after provider
  health returns (identity persists); Skipper fleet inspection for unhealthy
  computers; verify Settings -> Audit after suspected tampering; preserve
  Application Support before reinstalling; never bypass signature/notarization/
  Gatekeeper failures.

## Troubleshooting

- Button highlights but Continue does nothing: every visible question needs one
  selected option or typed answer; selection should survive live repaints.
- Skipper reports only #main: ask "what channels exist" — inventory comes from the
  native control plane, includes archived channels when requested.
- Gmail asks repeated questions: use `@skipper can we set up Gmail` or Connections
  -> Gmail; the native path must not open consecutive interviews.
- Model uses a disabled account: confirm disabled in Providers, reproduce one
  request, inspect Logs — disabled accounts should be absent, not merely fail
  first.
- Terminal and Files disagree: confirm prompt under /workspace; refresh Files after
  the command completes.
- Scheduled job didn't run: inspect Workflows/Board; ask Skipper to list
  obligations and reconcile the fleet; archived channels pause workflows.
- PDF preview blank: retry Open, then Download (authoritative fallback).

## Security summary

- Per-resident Apple Linux VMs, no Mac home mount (macOS native only).
- Skipper owns host/fleet/credential-broker/cross-channel authority; residents get
  task-scoped tools, never raw host credentials.
- Credentials and connectors are host-owned and minimally brokered.
- Workspace file mirrors are channel-scoped, size-bounded, symlink-contained.
- Agent interviews follow a narrow human-only policy.
- External skills: revision-pinned, bounded, scanned, hashed, wrapped.
- Operational history is locally tamper-evident (append-only SHA-256 chain).
- Releases are Developer ID signed, notarized, stapled, Gatekeeper verified.
- Report vulnerabilities privately via GitHub's "Report a vulnerability" on
  gitcommit90/1Helm. Only the latest release receives security fixes.

## Agent-first JSON CLI

    export HELM_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8123
    export HELM_TOKEN='a 1Helm session token'

    npm run helm -- channels
    printf '%s\n' '{"channel_id":2,"body":"Own this outcome and verify it."}' \
      | npm run helm -- message
    printf '%s\n' '{"channel_id":2,"name":"Weekly evidence","prompt":"Audit the launch and publish a verified status.","interval_seconds":604800}' \
      | npm run helm -- workflow-create
    npm run helm -- audit-verify

## FAQ (short answers)

- Free? MIT-licensed, open source, self-hosted; bring your own model accounts/keys.
- Data leaves the Mac? No hosted control plane; credentials host-owned; residents
  never receive tokens.
- Switching models? Identity, computer, memory, skills, files, obligations, threads
  all survive.
- Residents read my Mac? No — isolated VMs, no home mount (macOS native).
- Send email/texts? Gmail drafts only (send disabled); iMessage replies only within
  allowlisted conversations.
- Tutorial answers? Bounded outcome gate objects (max 3x, logged).
- App closed? Obligations persist and wake computers, but the Mac must be on.
- Windows/Linux? Headless compatibility only today; no native packages yet.
- Use the fabric from other tools? Yes — OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible /v1 endpoint
  with separate external keys.
